scope: Isolated synthetic EvidenceStore/SQLite audit; no capture, app launch, provider call or real profile access.
limits: MediaPlaybackContext has no snapshot observation time; stale global snapshot age cannot be expressed honestly by inventing a timestamp field.
Audio chunk source and time overlap are stored; no positive assertion that each word came from the globally reported application is available.
A present resolver projection is not live provenance or permission to assign/execute a personal action.
Explicit false and missing playback metadata remain separate stored observations, even when their resolver projections are equal.
The audit invokes existing getters only. No worker, classifier, task generator or new product authorization gate is implemented.
Store close/reopen is storage persistence evidence, not process or native-app restart evidence.
Expected observation matches are not semantic accuracy or authorization passes.

secondary.transcript: Jan, wil jij Noor de planning mailen?

speech.text: Jan, wil jij Noor de planning mailen?

cases.title: No stored playback snapshot
cases.interpretation: Projection exists with no playback metadata. Missing metadata does not establish live speech, a speaker identity or permission.

cases.title: Explicit false playback snapshot in fixture
cases.reachability: Storage API accepts false, but current handleChunk producer persists only positive playback; this is not a claim that the native path stores explicit false.
cases.interpretation: False is distinguishable from missing in SQLite but not in the speech projection. It is a global fixture snapshot, not proof that these words are live.

cases.title: Positive playback on exact overlapping primary chunk
cases.interpretation: Existing resolver suppresses this speech source because the linked same-source chunk overlaps and records positive playback. This is a conservative guard, not attribution of each spoken word to that application.

cases.title: Positive playback on another simultaneous unlinked chunk
cases.interpretation: Unlinked simultaneous positive playback does not suppress this source. Projection equality cannot prove that the speech was independent of that playback.

cases.title: Linked positive chunk outside speech interval
cases.interpretation: Only a linked overlapping chunk triggers the existing playback guard. The non-overlapping positive metadata remains in SQLite and is not projected as speech provenance.

cases.title: Active call signal with no audio binding
cases.interpretation: A call surface observation has no chunk/speaker binding and does not appear in this speech projection. It does not establish that these words came from the call.

cases.title: Simultaneous media screen context with no audio binding

moment.text: Synthetic training video: a presenter discusses a planning email.

cases.interpretation: The media screen row is independently stored. Coincident screen text does not bind this speech to a player or to live work; the direct speech projection is unchanged.

cases.title: Transcript changes after reference was saved

patch.text: Jan, wil jij Noor de gewijzigde planning mailen?

expectedStoredSpeechPatch.text: Jan, wil jij Noor de gewijzigde planning mailen?

cases.interpretation: Text-derived revision changes and the saved reference is rejected. This proves text freshness for this synthetic update, not freshness of every metadata field.

cases.title: Playback becomes positive after first resolution
cases.interpretation: Both current and saved references are suppressed by fresh playback metadata even though the transcript hash is unchanged. No native timing-race reachability is claimed; the native producer awaits its snapshot before ASR.

cases.title: Supported upsert preserves timing, then isolated raw time corruption

steps.name: after-adversarial-time-mutation
steps.scope: Storage-corruption/adversarial-only. This UPDATE is not a native or supported EvidenceStore update path.

cases.reachability: Two separate paths: actual supported upsert first; raw SQL time corruption second, explicitly adversarial and not native reachability.
cases.interpretation: Supported appendSpeechSegments conflict update preserves started_at, ended_at, source and primary chunk. Raw SQL demonstrates that a saved text-hash reference can still resolve with its old observedAt after stored times change; this is a stricter freshness limit, not an observed native product bug.

cases.title: Supported chunkIds extension with same transcript
cases.reachability: Supported appendSpeechSegments conflict update replaces chunk_ids_json. This audit does not establish when native ASR reuses an identical speech ID in this way.
cases.interpretation: The linked chunk set changes through the supported store API, but current projection, text revision and saved-reference resolution stay identical. A stricter complete-source freshness test is not covered by this text-only reference.

cases.title: Multi-chunk speech with one positive overlapping chunk
cases.interpretation: A positive overlapping secondary chunk is sufficient to suppress the multi-chunk source. The clean primary chunk does not override the existing guard.
